name: Acute Asthma Exacerbation
description: An acute or subacute worsening of asthma symptoms and airflow limitation, commonly presenting with increasing wheeze, shortness of breath, cough and chest tightness. Severe attacks may progress rapidly and require urgent assessment.
risk_factors: Tobacco smoke or air pollution exposure
Poor adherence to prescribed asthma controller therapy
physical_examination: Reduced air entry in severe airflow obstruction
recommended_investigations: Peak expiratory flow or spirometric assessment when clinically feasible
Clinical assessment of respiratory rate, heart rate and work of breathing
Arterial blood gas testing when severe respiratory compromise is suspected
Chest imaging when an alternative diagnosis or complication is suspected
red_flags: Inability to speak normally because of breathlessness
Markedly reduced air entry or a silent chest
contraindications: Severe or rapidly worsening asthma symptoms require urgent clinical assessment and should not be managed solely by automated decision support.

clinical_references.title: 2026 Summary Guide for Asthma Management and Prevention
